item.title: Dashboard
item.description:
Dashboard

The Dashboard is the default screen when you open the app. It shows real-time free parking space counts for both monitored locations.

Parking Cards

Each location is shown as a parking card containing:

Element Description
Location name GreenDay or Uni Wroc
Free spaces count Large number showing currently available spaces
≈ indicator Shown when the value is approximated (interpolated from nearby data points)
Original value Shown in parentheses below the approximated value: (orig: 23)
Data age Small text showing how fresh the data is (e.g. 2m ago, just now)

Data Age Colour Coding

The free-spaces number changes colour based on how fresh the data is:

item.title: Statistics
item.description:
Statistics

The Statistics screen shows a time-series chart of historical parking availability for both GreenDay and Uni Wroc.

Chart Overview

The chart plots free parking spaces over time. Two lines are drawn:

Line Parking lot
First colour (default: green) GreenDay
Second colour (default: blue) Uni Wroc

Interacting with the Chart

Zooming

  • Scroll (or pinch on touch devices) to zoom in/out on the time axis.
  • Use the zoom slider at the bottom of the chart to pan and zoom.
  • Zoom state is preserved when you switch colour palettes.

Tooltip

  • Hover (or tap) over the chart to see exact values for both parking lots at a given time.

Colour Palette Selector

The Palette selector in the header (visible on wider screens) lets you choose from four built-in colour schemes:

item.title: Settings
item.description:
Settings

The Settings screen lets you personalise the Free Parking Monitor app and get support.

Navigate to Settings by clicking ⚙️ Settings in the header from any screen.

Sections

App Info

Shows the current app version and a brief description of the application.

Color Vision Mode

Adjust the indicator colours (progress bars, status colours) for your colour vision needs.

Eight modes are available:

Mode Description
Normal (default) Standard green / orange / red palette
Protan Protanopia / Protanomaly – reduced red sensitivity; uses yellow/amber + blue
Deutan Deuteranopia / Deuteranomaly – green/red confusion; uses blue/orange/purple
Tritan Tritanopia / Tritanomaly – blue/yellow confusion; uses green/magenta/amber
Achrom Achromatopsia (monochromacy) – strong grayscale with monotonic luminance
HiCon High contrast – crisp tones for low-vision users
LowVis Low vision – highly saturated palette (AMD, diabetic retinopathy)
Cataracts Cataracts – cooler, higher-contrast tones

How to Select

  • Click any mode button. The active mode is highlighted with a coloured border.
  • Your selection is saved automatically in your browser (key: parking_cb_mode).
  • The colour change takes effect immediately on the Dashboard and Statistics chart.

Compatibility with Theme

All color vision modes work with both Light and Dark themes – each mode has optimised colour variants for both backgrounds.
